title: Condizionale presente
description: Formation of the present conditional and its uses: politeness, wishes, advice, hypothetical consequences and reported information.
objectives: Form the condizionale presente from the future stem.
Make polite requests (vorrei, potrebbe…) and give advice (dovresti).
Use the conditional for the consequence of a hypothetical condition.
Recognise the 'journalistic' conditional for unconfirmed information.

blocks.title: Future stem + -ei, -esti, -ebbe, -emmo, -este, -ebbero
blocks.text: The conditional uses exactly the same stem as the futuro, with its own endings: *parler-ei, sar-ei, vorr-ei, andr-ei*. Every irregularity of the future therefore reappears here.

blocks.title: noi: -emmo, not -emo
blocks.text: The noi forms of futuro and condizionale differ only by a double m: *parleremo* (we will speak) / *parleremmo* (we would speak). The difference is audible: the mm is pronounced long.

items: Politeness and attenuation: *Vorrei un caffè. Potrebbe aiutarmi? Mi daresti una mano?*
Advice and obligation softened: *Dovresti dormire di più.* (You ought to sleep more.)
Consequence of a hypothesis: *Se avessi tempo, leggerei di più.* (see the lesson on hypothetical sentences)
Opinion stated cautiously: *Direi che hai ragione.*
Unconfirmed or reported information, typical of journalism: *Secondo alcune fonti, il ministro sarebbe a Roma.* (The minister is reportedly in Rome.)

blocks.title: Never after se in a hypothesis
blocks.text: In the se-clause of a hypothetical sentence the standard language uses the congiuntivo, not the conditional: *Se potessi, verrei* — not *se potrei*. The conditional in the se-clause is heard in nonstandard speech.

examples.it: Vorrei un bicchiere d'acqua, per favore.
examples.en: I'd like a glass of water, please.
I'd like to live in the country.

examples.it: Se avessi una barca, andrei in Sardegna.
examples.en: If I had a boat, I'd go to Sardinia.
examples.note: Congiuntivo imperfetto in the se-clause, conditional in the main clause.

examples.it: Secondo il giornale, il ladro sarebbe scappato in Francia.
examples.en: According to the newspaper, the thief reportedly escaped to France.
examples.note: Conditional of reported information (here condizionale passato).

examples.en: We would gladly speak with him.

exercises.explanation: Conditional: -emmo (double m). andremo is the future, andassimo the congiuntivo imperfetto.

mistakes.message: andremo (one m) is the futuro: we will go. The conditional has -emmo.

exercises.prompt: What does *Il presidente sarebbe malato* mean in a newspaper?
options: The president is reportedly ill (not confirmed).
exercises.answer: The president is reportedly ill (not confirmed).
exercises.explanation: The journalistic conditional marks information the writer does not vouch for.
Standard Italian uses the congiuntivo imperfetto in the se-clause; the conditional goes in the main clause (verrei).

mistakes.message: The conditional is not used after se in standard Italian: se potessi.

exercises.prompt: Translate: You ought to sleep more. (tu)
exercises.explanation: dovere in the conditional = ought to / should.

exercises.text: Mi {0} (piacere) un gelato. {1} (Volere, io) anche un caffè. Voi {2} (venire) con noi?

summary: Same irregular stems as the futuro: sarei, avrei, vorrei, andrei, verrei, potrei, dovrei.
Uses: politeness, wishes, advice, hypothetical consequences, unconfirmed information.
Not after se in standard Italian: se potessi, verrei.

title: Condizionale passato and the future in the past
description: Unrealised past possibilities, and the condizionale passato as the standard 'future in the past'.
objectives: Express what would have happened, or should have happened, but did not.
Use the condizionale passato for a future seen from the past (disse che sarebbe venuto).
Avoid transferring the English/French/Spanish 'would + verb' pattern into reported speech.

blocks.title: Conditional of the auxiliary + participle
blocks.text: *avrei fatto, sarei andato/a*. Auxiliary choice and agreement as in the passato prossimo.

items: What would have happened: *Sarei venuto, ma ero malato.* (I would have come, but I was ill.)
Regret and reproach: *Avresti dovuto dirmelo.* (You should have told me.)
Polite past wishes: *Avrei voluto un tè.*
Consequence of a counterfactual condition: *Se fossi partito prima, sarei arrivato in tempo.*

blocks.title: Modal verbs
blocks.text: *avrei dovuto, avrei potuto, avrei voluto* + infinitive are extremely common: 'I should have / could have / would have liked to'. With an essere-verb infinitive, both *avrei dovuto partire* and *sarei dovuto partire* are standard (Accademia della Crusca); avere is increasingly frequent.

blocks.title: condizionale passato, not presente
blocks.text: To report, from a past point of view, an event that was then in the future, standard Italian uses the **condizionale passato**: *Marco ha detto che sarebbe venuto* (Marco said he would come) — even if the event may still happen. English 'would come', French *viendrait* and Spanish *vendría* use a simple conditional; Italian *verrebbe* in this sense is a common learner error.

blocks.caption: From direct to reported speech
rows: Ha detto che sarebbe venuto il giorno dopo.
Mi ha promesso che mi avrebbe scritto.

examples.it: Sarei venuta volentieri, ma dovevo lavorare.
examples.en: I would gladly have come, but I had to work.
You should have told me earlier.

examples.it: Marco ha detto che sarebbe arrivato alle otto.
examples.en: Marco said he would arrive at eight.
examples.note: Future in the past = condizionale passato.

examples.it: Ero sicuro che avrebbe vinto la tartaruga.
examples.en: I was sure the tortoise would win.
examples.note: Subject after the verb: la tartaruga.

examples.it: Se avessi saputo, ti avrei aiutato.
examples.en: If I had known, I would have helped you.
I would have liked to see the sea.

exercises.explanation: andare takes essere; the participle agrees with the subject.

exercises.prompt: Sara ha detto che ___ (venire) alla festa.
exercises.explanation: A future seen from a past point of view: condizionale passato. 'verrà' is possible only if the speaker stresses that the event is still in the future now; verrebbe is not standard here.

mistakes.message: Italian uses the condizionale passato for the future in the past: sarebbe venuta.

exercises.prompt: Translate: You should have told me. (tu)
exercises.explanation: condizionale passato of dovere + infinitive with the combined pronoun me lo attached (dirmelo).

exercises.text: «Ti scriverò.» → Mi ha promesso che mi {0}. «Pioverà.» → Pensavo che {1}.
exercises.explanation: Future in the past = condizionale passato. Weather verbs accept both auxiliaries.

exercises.prompt: *Sarei venuto, ma ero malato.* Did the speaker come?
exercises.explanation: The condizionale passato presents a possibility that was not realised.

exercises.prompt: Match each sentence with its function.
exercises.explanation: The condizionale passato covers unrealised wishes and obligations, the future in the past and reported information.

summary: Condizionale passato = conditional of avere/essere + participle.
Unrealised past possibilities, regrets, reproaches (avresti dovuto…).
The future in the past is the condizionale passato: disse che sarebbe venuto.
dovere/potere/volere + essere-verb infinitive: both avrei dovuto partire and sarei dovuto partire are standard.
